description: ArcolaAI fork of ssh-mcp-server. Renovate is driven by the self-hosted run in ArcolaAI/arcola-ai-platform (config.js lists this repo); it covers the four direct dependencies the fork still takes from the registry, which the fork pin in the estate's workstation manifest does not. Same 7-day release-age floor as every estate repo (the unpublish / malicious-publish window); merging is attended, never automerged. A bump changes package.json/package-lock.json only; build/ is unaffected, and the build-matches-source check proves it on the PR. Upstream (classfang/ssh-mcp-server) releases are watched separately from arcola-ai-platform workstation/upstream-watch.json.

MEASURED on the first live run (arcola-ai-platform run 35215789140, 2026-09-17T11:48Z): this repo has ISSUES DISABLED, so Renovate logs 'Cannot ensure issue because issues are disabled' and NO dependency dashboard can exist here. A dependencyDashboardApproval gate would therefore hold a major for ever with no surface to approve it on - the R13 dead-channel failure in its worst form, a channel that does not exist. So no rule here gates on the dashboard, and dependencyDashboard is off explicitly rather than failing every run. Majors arrive as their own labelled PR; the guard is the 7-day floor, the PR's own CI (build-matches-source + CodeQL) and an attended merge. The same run also warns 'Cannot access vulnerability alerts' HERE ONLY (the platform repo reads them fine, and a user token reads this repo's alerts fine), so the App's token cannot see Dependabot alerts on this repo: osvVulnerabilityAlerts is therefore set, which uses Renovate's own OSV datasource and needs no GitHub alert permission.

packageRules.description: Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs (ISMS-INC-001).

Majors get their own PR and a review label - the fork is cherry-pick territory, so a major on ssh2 or the MCP SDK is read against upstream before it moves. NOT dashboard-gated: issues are disabled on this repo, so there is no dashboard to approve it on (see the description above).
